newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel keeps currency basket composition.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel keeps currency basket composition.

text.p: The Bank of Israel announced on Wednesday that it will maintain the weights of the various currencies that make up the basket to which the shekel is pegged.
Since 1995 the central bank has annually reviewed the composition of the basket, comparing the weights of the currencies in it to the weights of the currencies in Israeli trade.
In 1995 and 1996 the central basket raised the weight of the dollar in the basket to reflect an increase in Israeli trade with dollar-bloc countries.
Currently, the dollar's weight is 60.1 percent; the Deutsche mark 21.3 percent; the pound sterling 8.2 percent; the French franc 5.1 percent and the yen 5.4 percent.

Until 1986 the Bank of Israel conducted exchange rate policy against the dollar. Since then it has valued the shekel against the basket of foreign countries, which reflects the composition of Israel's external trade.
